runs.question: Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
runs.answer:
[Turn 1 | session=ses_0916a23e2ffe8FwnPjbasYLUXb] Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
**Mainnet — 20 June 2026 (UTC)** — first-seen block arrival times:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total slots with data | 7,180 |
| Slot range | 14,590,799 – 14,597,998 |
| Time range | 00:00:11 – 23:59:59 UTC |
| **Avg first-seen arrival** | **1,710.4 ms** |
| Median (p50) arrival | 1,453 ms |
| p95 arrival | 3,126 ms |
| Fastest block arrival | 141 ms |
| Slowest block arrival | 5,249 ms |

Each row in the full result represents a slot with its `first_seen_arrival_ms` (the minimum `seen_slot_start_diff` across all observing nodes — i.e. the earliest time any node reported seeing that block after the slot started).

[Turn 2 | session=ses_0916a23e2ffe8FwnPjbasYLUXb] Plot the distribution of those arrival times as a chart.
Chart saved and uploaded. Here's the result:

**Distribution of first-seen block arrival times — Mainnet 2026-06-20**

URL: http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/b952623a5b33/20f384df-5112-4610-ace6-385cbd5cb383/arrival_distribution.png

The histogram (50 bins, 7,180 blocks) shows:
- **Peak** around ~1,200–1,500 ms — the most common first-seen arrival window
- **Long tail** trailing off past 3,000 ms, with a few outliers near 5,200 ms
- **Median** at 1,453 ms, mean at 1,710 ms — the distribution is right-skewed
- A few blocks were seen as fast as **141 ms** from slot start

The chart confirms the finding in the title: the vast majority of mainnet blocks are first picked up by at least one node within ~3 seconds of the slot beginning.
